problem: "a negative or positive gate voltage changes the width of a conducting channel" mixes the two families. A student may think an n-channel JFET can be biased with a positive gate voltage, which forward biases its gate junction.
fix: Split the sentence: in an n-channel JFET the gate voltage is negative (reverse bias), and in an n-channel enhancement MOSFET the gate voltage is positive (inversion layer).

problem: VGS(off) is equated with the pinch-off voltage VP without a sign convention. Many textbooks quote VP as a positive magnitude, VP = |VGS(off)|, so a student meeting VP = 4 V elsewhere will redo the square law with the wrong sign.
fix: Add: here VP means VGS(off) itself, so VP is negative for an n-channel JFET; some books quote VP as the positive magnitude |VGS(off)|.

problem: The saturation formula is given without the condition for reaching saturation (VDS ≥ VGS − VT, the overdrive voltage). Quiz Q5 also assumes saturation without stating it, so the student cannot check the assumption.
fix: Add one line before the formula: the MOSFET is in saturation when VDS ≥ VGS − VT, where VGS − VT is the overdrive voltage in V; below this it behaves as a voltage-controlled resistor in the triode region.
